messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — Acme ticket: their webhook success rate dropped from ~99% to ~60% starting 03:45 UTC. They say their firewall shows a mix of our allowed IPs and some IPs they don't recognize.
maria_support: Customer pasted a few source IPs: 35.192.11.45, 35.192.11.46 (expected), but also 34.210.1.2 and 34.210.1.3 which they say are not on their allowlist. They saw both 200 and 403 responses for different retries.
devon_eng: Thanks. Any example request/response or curl output? Are errors TLS-related or connection resets? Also which VPC/private deployment is this tied to? (customer says private deployment in us-east-1)
maria_support: Here's the snippet from their Ops team:
```
$ curl -v -H 'X-Request-Id: r-7c1' https://hooks.acme.com/w/e
* Connected to hooks.acme.com (34.210.1.2) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 handshake, received certificate
> GET /w/e HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{...}
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 403
```
maria_support: They also included netflow showing many source IPs outside the ~35.192.11.0/24 block we previously shared.
devon_eng: That looks like a partial SNAT rotation — some worker nodes switched to different egress IPs. If the customer allowlist is pinned to a tiny set of IPs this will cause intermittent 403s. @sanjay_netops can you check NAT/egress assignment for the customer's private VPC around 03:40-03:50 UTC?
sanjay_netops: Looking now. I see a scheduled host maintenance at 03:39 that triggered an AZ failover in that VPC's NAT cluster. During the rebalance, the SNAT mapping moved a subset of flows onto a second NAT pool (egress IPs 34.210.1.0/31) that we hadn't advertised to the customer. Rolling logs:
```
03:39:21 /nat-controller : reassign pool -> vpc-0abc: from eip-35.192.11.45 to dynamic-eip-34.210.1.2
03:39:22 /nat-controller : reassign pool -> vpc-0abc: from eip-35.192.11.46 to dynamic-eip-34.210.1.3
```
sanjay_netops: TL;DR — pool rebalance put ~20% of SNAT onto transient egress IPs. Not ideal.
devon_eng: Can we 1) stop rebalance to that VPC, 2) pin static EIPs for their NAT gateway, and 3) provide the full list of observed egress IPs to the customer so they can update their allowlist? Any impact to latency/throughput?
sanjay_netops: I'm pinning their NAT to the previously advertised EIPs now (reassigning Elastic IPs back). Should be done in ~5m. No throughput impact expected. I'll also export the connection sample for debugging.
nat-bot: NAT assignment change initiated for vpc-0abc by sanjay_netops at 03:46:12 UTC. Old pool: [35.192.11.45, 35.192.11.46], transient pool: [34.210.1.2, 34.210.1.3].
deploy-bot: NAT pin rollback applied (job id nat-rollback-191111). Completed 03:50:18 UTC.
maria_support: I shared the full observed ip list with Acme and asked them to broaden allowlist to the /24 while we investigate longer-term config. They replied that their security policy requires explicit IPs — asking us to guarantee stable egress.
devon_eng: Action items: 1) ops to file config change to pin EIPs for customer on all planned maintenance windows 2) support to offer customer either reserved EIPs or route via customer-managed NAT (VPC egress) 3) infra to add alert when <=95% of flows use advertised ip set.
sanjay_netops: Filed infra ticket INF-3251 to add monitor — I'll add the maintenance guardrail. Also adding runbook step: when rebalance happens, signal impacted customers and suspend rolling immediately for private VPCs with allowlists.
maria_support: Customer confirmed success after we pinned EIPs and their webhook success rate climbed back to 99%. They left a follow-up asking for a postmortem and a note in onboarding docs about allowlist size recommendations.
devon_eng: Thanks team. Recommend we also update customer onboarding checklist: "If you use private VPC webhooks, allowlist at least /24 or request pinned EIPs (recommended for strict policies)." Closing thread once INF-3251 and the customer postmortem are created.
